title: Wrap executable top-level Python code in func main
description: Executable top-level Python statements must become a Go main function body. Go file scope only allows declarations.
python_signal: module-level input(), print(), assignments, or control flow outside any function
compile_error_signatures: syntax error: non-declaration statement outside function body

title: Drop unused imports before emitting Go
description: Any imported Go package that is not referenced is a compile error.
python_signal: translation added an import speculatively

title: fmt.Scan and fmt.Fscan return a count and an error
description: Go scanning APIs return two values. Assign both or discard the count explicitly.
python_signal: input parsing translated to fmt.Scan or fmt.Fscan
go_pattern:
_, err := fmt.Fscan(reader, &n)
if err != nil { return }
compile_error_signatures: assignment mismatch: 1 variable but fmt.Fscan returns 2 values

title: strconv.Atoi returns (int, error)
description: Atoi does not behave like Python int(); it returns two values that must be handled.
python_signal: string-to-int conversion in source
go_pattern:
n, err := strconv.Atoi(text)
if err != nil { return 0 }

title: A parameter named strings hides the strings package
description: If the Go signature already has a parameter named strings, strings.Join refers to the slice value, not the stdlib package.
python_signal: signature parameter named strings
compile_error_signatures: strings.Join undefined (type []string has no field or method Join)
strings.HasPrefix undefined (type []string has no field or method HasPrefix)

title: A parameter named sort hides the sort package
description: If the Go signature binds sort as a value name, sort.Slice no longer refers to the stdlib package.
python_signal: signature parameter named sort
go_pattern:
items := sortInput
sort.Slice(items, func(i, j int) bool { return items[i] < items[j] })

title: A parameter named fmt hides the fmt package
description: If the Go signature binds fmt as a local name, fmt.Printf no longer refers to the stdlib package.
python_signal: signature parameter named fmt

title: math.Gcd is not in the Go standard library
description: There is no math.Gcd in the Go stdlib. Implement gcd inline.
python_signal: Python uses math.gcd or an equivalent gcd helper expectation

title: strings.Reverse is not in the Go standard library
description: There is no strings.Reverse in the Go stdlib. Reverse bytes or runes manually.
python_signal: string reversal in source

title: Emit every helper function the translated logic calls
description: If the translated function body calls a helper, that helper must also be defined in the emitted Go file.
python_signal: multiple source helpers or nested helper-style decomposition in the Python source
go_pattern:
func helper(x int) int { return x + 1 }

func Solve(x int) int { return helper(x) }
avoid_pattern: func Solve(x int) int { return helper(x) }

title: Mixed int and float arithmetic needs explicit widening
description: Python mixes ints and floats freely. Go requires explicit conversion before arithmetic.
python_signal: int arithmetic mixed with float literals or float results

title: Convert ints to strings explicitly
description: Python concatenates str(int) easily. Go needs strconv.Itoa or fmt.Sprintf.
python_signal: number concatenated into a string
compile_error_signatures: cannot use n as string value
invalid operation: mismatched types int and string

title: Whitespace-token input needs a token reader
description: When Python reads tokenized numeric input, use Scanner with ScanWords or Fscan consistently rather than line-oriented reads.
python_signal: input().split() or map(int, input().split())
runtime_error_signatures: panic: runtime error: index out of range

title: Large token streams may require a bigger Scanner buffer
description: Default Scanner buffers can be too small for competitive-programming style input. Increase the buffer when scanning large tokens.
python_signal: bulk stdin reads or potentially long tokens

title: print(x, y) requires exact separator behavior
description: Python print with multiple args emits one space and a trailing newline. Use an explicit format when exact stdout matters.
python_signal: print with multiple arguments

title: Float output often needs an explicit format specifier
description: Python str(float) and Go default float formatting are not always byte-equivalent. Use the required precision explicitly.
python_signal: float values printed or converted to string

title: Rewrite xs[-1] as xs[len(xs)-1]
description: Go does not support negative indices. The last element must be indexed explicitly.
python_signal: negative subscript xs[-1]

title: Rewrite xs[-2] as xs[len(xs)-2]
description: Go does not support negative indices. The second-last element must be indexed explicitly.
python_signal: negative subscript xs[-2]

title: Python xs[:] copy semantics require an explicit Go copy before mutation
description: Python xs[:] allocates a new list. In Go, assigning a slice aliases the backing array. Copy first if the new slice is later mutated.
python_signal: xs[:] or similar slice-copy expression followed by mutation

title: Go map iteration order is not Python dict order
description: If output depends on dict traversal order, a raw Go map loop is wrong. Preserve order explicitly.
python_signal: dictionary iteration where output order matters

title: sorted(..., key=...) usually needs a stable Go sort
description: Python sorted is stable. If equal keys must keep source order, use sort.SliceStable or decorate with original indices.
python_signal: sorted call with a derived key

title: list.sort(key=...) usually needs a stable Go sort
description: Python list.sort is stable. Preserve tie order in Go when the benchmark depends on it.
python_signal: in-place sort call with a key

title: Python // with negatives is not Go /
description: Python floor division rounds toward negative infinity. Go integer division truncates toward zero.
python_signal: // used where operands may be negative

title: Return []T{} instead of nil when Python returns []
description: When the source returns an empty list and the Go signature returns a slice, prefer an empty slice literal unless nil is explicitly acceptable.
python_signal: return [] from a function whose Go return type is []T
